title: Jupiter’s Storms and Moons
objective: After this level you can describe the Great Red Spot and Jupiter’s four large moons.
summary: The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth. Jupiter’s four big moons range from volcanic Io to giant Ganymede.

cards.headline: Jupiter has a storm bigger than Earth that has lasted for centuries.
The Great Red Spot
cards.body: Jupiter’s Great Red Spot is a giant storm wider than Earth. Astronomers have watched it for more than 150 years, and it’s still spinning, though it has been shrinking over the past century.

cards.headline: Four worlds of their own
cards.body: Jupiter has dozens of moons, but Galileo’s four are by far the largest, and wildly different. Io is the most volcanically active world in the solar system. Ganymede is the largest moon of all, bigger than the planet Mercury. Callisto is one of the most heavily cratered worlds known. And Europa? That’s the next level.

cards.headline: Jupiter system: explored
learned: The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth
It has been observed for over 150 years
Io is the most volcanic world in the solar system
Ganymede is the largest moon, bigger than Mercury

questions.prompt: What is Jupiter’s Great Red Spot?

options.label: A giant volcano on its surface
A shadow cast by one of its moons
options.rationale: Moon shadows are small and move quickly.

options.label: An impact crater from an asteroid
options.rationale: Jupiter has no surface for craters.

questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm, wider than Earth, observed for more than 150 years.

questions.prompt: Which of Jupiter’s moons is bigger than the planet Mercury?

options.label: Callisto, the cratered one
options.rationale: Callisto is large, but Ganymede is bigger.

questions.explanation: Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system and is bigger than Mercury.

questions.prompt: From Level 25: Galileo saw Jupiter’s four large moons as tiny dots. What do we know about Io today?

options.label: It is the coldest object in the solar system
options.rationale: Io is famous for heat, not cold.

options.label: It is the most volcanically active world in the solar system
It is made entirely of water ice
It orbits Jupiter backwards
options.rationale: Io orbits in the usual direction.

questions.explanation: Galileo’s tiny dot Io turned out to be the most volcanically active world in the solar system.
